chunks: My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washa, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

When the boy reaches his maturity at thirteen years of age and enters his fourteenth year, whatever is incumbent upon the sexually mature becomes incumbent upon him, whether he has had a seminal emission or not; his bad deeds are recorded and his good deeds are recorded, and he is permitted to manage all his property unless he is weak-minded or foolish.

key_terms.الْمُحْتَلِمِينَ: the sexually mature (those who have had seminal emission)

ai.seo_question: At what age does a boy become legally responsible for religious duties and property management in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this hadith to establish thirteen lunar years as the definitive age of *bulugh* (puberty) for boys, emphasizing that legal accountability (*taklif*) and financial capacity (*ahliyyah*) commence at this specific milestone regardless of physical signs like seminal emission. This ruling out mental immaturity. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that chronological age serves as the primary objective criterion for assuming religious duties and managing property.
